- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model often overpredicts downward moves; reduce forecast slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 70+), overshooting true price by 1–3% in next 3–5 days; apply dampening factor to spike-driven forecasts.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon; if forecast is 2–3σ above recent mean, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days, model lags in adjusting; add 0.3–0.7% upward bias to forecast starting day 4.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates long-term upward trends (especially post-2024-07-10); add 0.5–1.5% cumulative bias toward higher end of range if sentiment remains positive.
